brief: Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities desk recap of the firm's Communacopia and Technology Conference, 260+ companies over four days. Sentiment read as hopeful rather than unanimously bullish, with clients wanting to add back tech because positioning had come off too far, and the desk's prime brokerage data confirms it. Hedge funds net bought US TMT in 10 of the last 11 sessions, a trailing two-week long-buying pace that is the largest since June 2025 and in the 97th percentile over five years. Five takeaways. Coding stays the core AI use case and the market underestimates the ARPU expansion coding alone can deliver. Cybersecurity is the next major use case, with CrowdStrike and Palo Alto named as the plays. Semis positioning looks too light and a poll of 12 managers drifted more constructive. The debate is moving from who owns the capex benefit toward who owns the application layer. Consumer datapoints from Visa, eBay, Airbnb and Etsy remain stable. The counterpoint is preserved: if open-source models already deliver enough efficiency for mostly simple workloads, 2028 capex may fall short of what is priced. Separately, GS now expects a Fed hike Wednesday versus a hold previously, with the market pricing 90%.
